theory.intro: A **standard normal table** lists $P(Z<c)$, the area under the curve to the **left** of a non-negative $z$-score $c$. Every other region is built from those values using the complement, a subtraction, or the symmetry of the curve.
facts: The table gives $P(Z<c)$, the area to the left of $c$, for non-negative values of $c$.
$P(Z>c) = 1 - P(Z<c)$, because the two areas together make up the whole area of $1$.
$P(a<Z<b) = P(Z<b) - P(Z<a)$, so a middle strip is a difference of two left-hand areas.
If an unstandardised score $x$ is given, first find $z = \dfrac{x-\mu}{\sigma}$, then use the table.
If an expected count is asked for, use the **expected frequency** $f = np$: the number of items $n$ times the probability $p$, rounded as the question requires.
steps: If an unstandardised score is given, convert it to a $z$-score using $z = \dfrac{x-\mu}{\sigma}$
Shade the required region under the curve
Read $P(Z<c)$ from the table and adjust it to the region wanted
If an expected count is asked for, multiply the probability by $n$ and round as required

workedExamples.question_text:
For a standard normal random variable $Z$, find $P(Z<0.48)$ using this table.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline z&0.48\\\hline P(Z<z)&0.6844\\\hline\end{array}$

For a standard normal random variable $Z$, find $P(Z>1.47)$ using this table.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|}\hline z&1.47\\\hline P(Z<z)&0.9292\\\hline\end{array}$

For a standard normal random variable $Z$, find $P(0.45<Z<1.65)$ using this table.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline z&0.45&1.65\\\hline P(Z<z)&0.6736&0.9505\\\hline\end{array}$

For a standard normal random variable $Z$, find $P(-1.72<Z<-0.56)$ using this table.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline z&0.56&1.72\\\hline P(Z<z)&0.7123&0.9573\\\hline\end{array}$

For a standard normal random variable $Z$, find $P(-0.73<Z<1.46)$ using this table.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline z&0.73&1.46\\\hline P(Z<z)&0.7673&0.9279\\\hline\end{array}$

The masses of $1200$ packets are normally distributed with a mean of $250$ g and a standard deviation of $10$ g. Find the probability that a randomly chosen packet has a mass between $242$ g and $263$ g, then find the expected number of such packets. Round the count to the nearest whole packet.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline z&0.80&1.30\\\hline P(Z<z)&0.7881&0.9032\\\hline\end{array}$

Examination marks are normally distributed with a mean of $55$ and a standard deviation of $12$. Use the closest probability in the table to find the approximate mark separating the top $15\%$ from the remaining marks. Give your answer to one decimal place.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline z&1.03&1.04&1.05\\\hline P(Z<z)&0.8485&0.8508&0.8531\\\hline\end{array}$

Completion times for a task are normally distributed with a mean of $80$ seconds and a standard deviation of $15$ seconds. Use the closest probability in the table to find the approximate time below which the fastest $25\%$ of times fall. Give your answer to one decimal place.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline z&0.66&0.67&0.68\\\hline P(Z<z)&0.7454&0.7486&0.7517\\\hline\end{array}$

development.question_text:
The masses of watermelons are normally distributed with a mean of $4.5$ kg and a standard deviation of $0.8$ kg.

$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|}\hline z & 0.75 & 1.50 & 2.25 \\ \hline P(Z<z) & 0.7734 & 0.9332 & 0.9878 \\ \hline\end{array}$
Find the probability that a randomly chosen watermelon has a mass less than $5.7$ kg.

The number of daily visitors to a museum is normally distributed with a mean of $480$ and a standard deviation of $75$.

mastery.question_text:
A machine fills bottles with volumes that are normally distributed with a mean of $380$ mL and a standard deviation of $8$ mL.
A bottle is rejected if it holds less than $360$ mL.
Part of a standard normal table of $P(Z<z)$ is shown.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline z & 2.00 & 2.50 \\ \hline P(Z<z) & 0.9772 & 0.9938 \\ \hline\end{array}$
In a production run of $3500$ bottles, how many are expected to be rejected? Round to the nearest whole bottle.

The marks in an examination are normally distributed with a mean of $62$ and a standard deviation of $14$.
Part of a standard normal table of $P(Z<z)$ is shown.
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline z & 1.26 & 1.27 & 1.28 & 1.29 \\ \hline P(Z<z) & 0.8962 & 0.8980 & 0.8997 & 0.9015 \\ \hline\end{array}$
Using the table, find the approximate minimum mark a candidate needs in order to be in the top $10\%$. Give your answer to one decimal place.

$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline z & 0.80 & 1.00 \\ \hline P(Z<z) & 0.7881 & 0.8413 \\ \hline\end{array}$
How many workers are expected to travel between $12.8$ km and $24.5$ km? Round to the nearest whole worker.
